counterfactual_missing_items: Etiologic workup for metabolic or autoimmune neuropathy
decisive_items: recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation, alternating with intermittent diarrhea
CT scan showed small-bowel dilation (approximately 23 mm in diameter) consistent with obstruction
exploratory laparotomy “showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions.”
response.rationale: R5 is supported by the characteristic chronic obstructive symptoms, radiological findings of small-bowel dilation without mechanical cause on laparotomy, and failure of conservative and gluten-free trials. R4 (short bowel syndrome) is implausible because there is no history of extensive bowel resection; the weight loss and vitamin deficiencies are nonspecific and also occur in pseudo-obstruction. R5 directly accounts for the functional obstruction seen on imaging and surgical exclusion of mechanical causes.

rejected.why: Explicitly contradicted by 'including any evidence of celiac disease' and failure of gluten-free diet.
Lacks protein-losing enteropathy features (e.g., edema, lymphopenia) and does not explain the obstructive dilation and surgical findings.
Alcohol use is incidental; symptoms began after cholecystectomy and continued despite cessation, and there is no evidence specific to liver disease causing obstruction.
